prompt: Turn this flat diagram into a close-up texture photograph of the curtain wall of an old castle built of large dark granite blocks, three metres across. The whole image is a close-up of the flat surface itself, filling the frame edge to edge, seen exactly face-on: no edges, no corners, no roof, no ground, no sky, no horizon and no surroundings. Keep the composition exactly: every shape stays where it is, at the same size and in the same colour family. Each block shape becomes one large, roughly dressed, rock-faced dark grey granite block with a chisel-worked, weathered face, laid in level courses of slightly different heights, and the thin dark lines between them become narrow recessed joints of dark lime mortar. The stone is evenly weathered and darkened by soot and rain, with only faint differences in tone from block to block and no growth on it. Flat overcast diffuse daylight, no cast shadows, no specular highlights, uniform exposure from edge to edge, no perspective, no vignette, sharp focus everywhere. Photorealistic, high detail, natural muted colours of a cold, damp late-autumn borderland.
